newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr, forward premia fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr, forward premia fall.

text.p: The India rupee strengthened on liquidation of long positions by banks to end Tuesday at 35.685/695 against the day's opening 35.72/73, dealers said.
"The Reserve Bank of India did not buy dollars today contrary to market expectations," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "Banks liquidated their long positions and this pushed up the rupee."

Dealers said premia on forward dollars fell further on Tuesday. "Expectations of improving domestic liquidity are pushing premia down," a dealer said. The premia for six-month dollars ended Tuesday around 9.75 percent annualised, down from Monday's 9.52 percent against 9.85 percent, he said.
